subject: Error due to package loading method

messages.author: 2dc50513792871a4
messages.subject: Error due to package loading method
parts:
Hi,

This may have come up before but I had difficulty searching the topic. I thought it might be worth sharing the following observation. Upon deploying an app to shinyapps.io, it first worked when I loaded packages like this:

suppressMessages({
library(shiny)
library(shinyBS)
library(shinyjs)
library(leaflet)
library(rgdal)
library(raster)
library(data.table)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
})

I tidied things up a bit and redeployed the app with my script loading packages like this:

pkgs <- list("shiny", "shinyBS", "shinyjs", "leaflet", "rgdal", "raster", "data.table", "dplyr", "tidyr", "ggplot2")
suppressMessages(lapply(pkgs, function(x) library(x, character.only=T)))

It failed, saying there was no 'shinyBS' package. I then moved that one out of the list, using the standard library(shinyBS) call and sure enough the next redeployment complained that the next package still in the list, 'shinyjs', was missing. Apparently packages cannot be properly detected when loaded with lapply on a list of package names. I don't know if I'd call this a bug or real issue, but it seems worth mentioning in case others encounter it.

Matt

messages.author: e84e7628b5f8a3e1
messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Error due to package loading method
parts:
Matt,

You are correct: the dependency detection is only sophisticated enough to detect packages that are loaded explicitly with require/library or implicitly with double to triple colons. The current method does a simple grep of the sources looking for those patterns. Unfortunately, it would likely require a far more advanced method to detect package using your method, which is not something we're looking at doing currently.

Sorry for the inconvenience,
Best,
-Andy
